newsitem.title: BELARUS: Clashes erupt at Belarus anti-union protest.
newsitem.headline: Clashes erupt at Belarus anti-union protest.

text.p: Police and pro-independence protesters clashed in the Belarussian capital on Wednesday after President Alexander Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed an outline Union Treaty.
Police blocked protesters from marching on the Russian embassy in Minsk and then laid into the crowd with truncheons as some activists started throwing stones.
Witnesses said police beat protesters at random and made about 100 arrests at the meeting, which had not been sanctioned by authorities. At least three journalists were among those detained.
One elderly man fell unconscious to the ground and was driven off in one of at least two ambulances called to the scene.
Some policemen also appeared to be hurt from stones hurled by protesters fearing union with Russia will return Belarus to domination by Moscow after five years of independence from the Soviet Union.
Similar protests against Lukashenko's pro-Moscow policies and crackdowns on demonstrations and the media have led to clashes in the past.
